questions.a: 'I will work harder' (also 'Napoleon is always right')

questions.q: Which pig persuades the animals with clever speeches?

passage.title: Power and responsibility
paras: Every school, club and country needs leaders. The question is not whether someone will hold power, but how that power will be checked.

A captain who listens to the team, explains decisions and admits mistakes earns trust that lasts. A captain who picks only friends, ignores complaints and blames others may win a match, but loses the team.

questions.q: Give two things the good captain does.
questions.a: Any two: listens to the team; explains decisions; admits mistakes

questions.q: How does the writer use contrast to make the point?
questions.a: Two captains are set side by side: one 'earns trust that lasts', the other 'loses the team'; the contrast shows that fairness and accountability matter more than winning

questions.q: Rewrite in the active voice: 'The windmill was destroyed by the storm.'
Add a cohesive device to link these sentences: 'The animals worked hard. The pigs grew fat.'
questions.a: For example: 'The animals worked hard; meanwhile, the pigs grew fat.'

questions.q: How does Orwell present the abuse of power in Animal Farm? Use PEEDL: Point, Evidence, Explain, Develop, Link.
questions.a: Award up to 10: argued point (2), apt short evidence (2), explanation of methods (2), development such as context (Stalin, the Russian Revolution) or an alternative reading (2), link to the question (2).
